Create a map chart

Source: R/highmaps.R
hcmap.Rd

Draw a packaged country map offline, load another map by its Highcharts collection path, or supply a GeoJSON or TopoJSON list.

Usage

hcmap(
  map = "custom/world",
  download_map_data = TRUE,
  data = NULL,
  value = NULL,
  joinBy = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

map

A two-letter country code (case-insensitive), a collection path such as "countries/jp/jp-all" or "custom/world", or a loaded map list. See hc_maps() for installed identifiers. Country codes and their matching collection paths use the same local file.

download_map_data

For maps outside the package, download the map in R (TRUE, the default) or attach the CDN script to the widget (FALSE).

data

Optional data to make a choropleth, in case of use the joinBy and value are needed.

value

A string value with the name of the variable to chart.

joinBy

What property to join the map and df.

...

Additional shared arguments for the data series (https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/series).

Examples


hcmap("jp")


hcmap("custom/south-america", showInLegend = FALSE)


hcmap("custom/world-robinson-lowres", data = subset(world_income, year == 2024),
  value = "gni_per_capita",
  joinBy = c("iso-a3", "iso3")
)



# Read a local GeoJSON or TopoJSON file and plot its boundaries.
path <- system.file("extdata", "districts.topo.json", package = "highcharter")
map <- jsonlite::read_json(path, simplifyVector = FALSE)
hcmap(map, showInLegend = FALSE)
